solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inoculant worked non-stop

indicators.note: letters that are worked are kneaded into a new shape

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A vaccine that did its job around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'worked' as 'was effective', but it is the instruction to rework INOCULANT, which uses exactly the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is continual never pauses.

clue.text: Stop talking to leader of union supporting Conservative grandee

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, the supporting piece sits beneath what it holds up

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
first letter of 'union'
a toff is a posh, upper-class person

explanation.surface: Snubbing a Tory bigwig who has been backed by a trade union leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue U 'supporting' C puts U beneath C. Toff is British slang for a well-to-do, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: you cut off a friend when you end contact and refuse to speak with them.

clue.text: Nosy neighbours always saw a lot at first

indicators.note: take each word at its first letter

parts.note: first letters of Neighbours, Always, Saw, A, Lot

explanation.surface: Prying neighbours who always seem to see everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosy' wants to mean prying, which is what the surface is about; here it means 'of the nose', as nasal does.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful literal reading: nosy taken as 'to do with the nose' is what nasal means.

clue.text: Wishful thinker that is accepting Muhammad, say

indicators.note: one piece accepts another inside it

parts.note: id est, Latin for 'that is', written i.e.
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

explanation.surface: Someone full of hopes who embraces the teachings of a great figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious reading of Muhammad is the misdirection; it is the boxer Muhammad Ali. 'That is' must be spelt out in full Latin, not as IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: an idealist chases how things ought to be, often hoping against reality.

clue.text: Aunt regarded university bad for student

indicators.note: letters gone bad are spoilt, out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An aunt who thinks going to university is a poor choice for a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'bad for student' the aunt's opinion; 'bad' is the anagram signal, and 'for' just points to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by a broader term: an undergraduate is one kind of student, working towards a first degree.

clue.text: Circuits fail to maintain standard we're told

indicators.note: what we are told we hear, so the answer sounds like the wordplay

parts.note: to lapse is to slip below a standard

explanation.surface: Electrical circuits that fall short of the required standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuits' suggests electronics; here it means rounds of a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the racing sense: each time round a track is a circuit.

clue.text: Image most choose

indicators.note: most of a word is the word less its last letter

parts.note: PICK = choose, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Picking the picture most people would choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' reads as 'the majority', but it trims PICK to PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal abbreviation: pic is short for picture, any image.

clue.text: Gift despatched in advance

parts.note: pre- means before, in advance
despatched = sent

explanation.surface: A gift posted early.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as 'sent early', and the wordplay says the same with the pieces in the other order.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the birthday or Christmas sense of something given.

clue.text: Produce echo within wooden box

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box
Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: Making a sound reverberate inside a wooden crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echo' looks like a sound bouncing round the box; it is just the letter E from the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as a verb: to bring something into being.

clue.text: Tea's temperature affected flavour

indicators.note: letters affected by something are altered

parts.note: tea's read as TEAS
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: How hot the tea was changed the way it tasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, so 'Tea’s' supplies four letters, and 'affected' reads as a verb in the surface but shuffles them with T.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the flavour of food or drink is its taste on the tongue.

clue.text: Introduce power to remove exhaust

indicators.note: a piece introduced to another is put into it
gives the destination of the introduced piece

parts.note: to delete is to remove
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Fitting more power to get rid of exhaust fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a noun about fumes; it is the verb meaning use up.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to use up resources until none are left.

clue.text: Traditional belief family role is changing

indicators.note: the letters of ROLE change their order

parts.note: your folk are your family
ROLE rearranged

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned ideas about who does what at home are shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'family role' as one phrase about gender roles; the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: folklore is the body of customs and beliefs handed down in a community.

clue.text: Amphibian beginning to wriggle in trap

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a net is a trap
first letter of 'wriggle'

explanation.surface: A newt starting to squirm once caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a caught creature starting to squirm; 'beginning to' takes just one letter of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the newt is one example of an amphibian, alongside frogs and toads.

clue.text: Protest about one traitorous US politician

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
c = circa, about
a rat is a traitor, one who betrays

explanation.surface: A demonstration against a politician seen as a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is not a container instruction here but C, short for circa, as in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Democrat belongs to one of the two main US parties.

clue.text: Religious education's pressing being born again

parts.note: RE = religious education, plus the 's
pressing = urgent

explanation.surface: Religious teaching is urgently needed for those being born again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born again' points to evangelical religion to match the surface; the answer only means reviving. RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: something resurgent is rising again, as if reborn.

clue.text: Unrestrained harangue involving a member of parliament

indicators.note: one piece involves another, taking it inside

parts.note: a rant is a harangue
a as itself
MP = member of parliament

explanation.surface: A wild tirade that drags in a parliamentarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a politician getting an earful; the harangue is only the outer shell, split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: growth or behaviour that is rampant runs wild, unchecked.

clue.text: Continue to feel tired? This may be about alcohol

parts.note: to flag is to tire
to go on is to continue, as in 'on!'

explanation.surface: Keeping going while worn out — maybe drink is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: 'about alcohol' means physically around it, as a vessel is. The pieces come in the reverse of clue order, with 'to' as glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for wine or beer, so it is literally around alcohol.

clue.text: Can see about spiritualist's meeting

indicators.note: letters turned about are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: A medium announcing they can see what surrounds the sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can see about' reads as 'will deal with'; 'about' is the signal to rearrange CAN SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a seance is a gathering where a medium tries to reach the dead.

clue.text: Insolence about male's lameness

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, another

parts.note: lip = cheek, insolence
M is the abbreviation for male
surface padding, the possessive glue before the definition

explanation.surface: Cheeky talk about a man's disability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lip' for cheeky talk is a British idiom: 'Don't give me any lip.'
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym as nouns: a limp is the uneven walk that lameness causes.

clue.text: Throw one's weight behind Scottish barrister

definitions.meaning: a verb phrase meaning support or champion
the title used in Scotland for a courtroom lawyer

explanation.surface: Backing a lawyer from north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scottish law, advocates are the equivalent of English barristers, the lawyers who argue in the higher courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to champion a cause, and a regional noun for a Scottish barrister.

clue.text: Friend since penning note

indicators.note: one piece pens, encloses, another

parts.note: ago = since, before now
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pal who has been writing a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, which suits 'note', but it means enclosing, as sheep are penned.
explanation.definitionFit: Loanword: amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English.

clue.text: Part of shoe pinched, losing time

indicators.note: the piece named next is taken away

parts.note: pinched = stole
T is the abbreviation for time; removed

explanation.surface: A shoe that pinched until it wore in over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' reads as a tight shoe; it is slang for stole.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by part: the underside of a shoe, the bit that meets the ground.

clue.text: US breakfast loaf endlessly cooked by nan

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter
the letters are cooked into a new order

parts.note: nan and gran are both grandmother
LOAF without its last letter, LOA, cooked into OLA

explanation.surface: Grandma bakes a loaf, American breakfast-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nan' is not the Indian bread, tempting beside 'loaf' and 'cooked': it is British for grandmother, GRAN, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Granola, toasted oats with nuts and fruit, is a breakfast food mainly called that in the US.

clue.text: Shower reportedly sit on the throne

indicators.note: a report is heard, so the answer sounds like the wordplay

parts.note: a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: Someone showering, or perhaps sitting on the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The throne' is British slang for the toilet, and a shower is in the bathroom, but the throne is a monarch's.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as monarch, to occupy the throne.

clue.text: Fanatic beheaded king once

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: Cnut (Canute), king of England, Denmark and Norway, without its first letter C

explanation.surface: A zealot who executed a former monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' suggests regicide; here it is the king's name that loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in 'a fitness nut'.

clue.text: Conductor's chosen baton perhaps used with energy

parts.note: the elect are the chosen, as in 'president-elect'
a baton is one kind of rod
E is the symbol for energy
surface padding that joins the last piece on

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor's chosen baton, wielded with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all orchestra, but the conductor is electrical. The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves.
